specification.problem: Simulate a disordered 2D discrete-time (split-step) quantum walk on a small periodic lattice with reflecting links cut along a straight A-to-B line, and estimate the arrival probability P_B(T) at B for cut versus uncut walks with identical static disorder.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: 4x4 periodic lattice (2 qubits per axis), 2 coin qubits (one per axis), 6 qubits total, no ancilla. A=(0,0), B=(2,0) on the x axis; the cut is on the horizontal links of the line y=0. Static random disorder angles come from a fixed seed. T is a few times the A-B distance. Out of scope: the periodically driven Hamiltonian realization, the quasienergy winding invariant computation, the Chern number, and large-lattice scaling.

symbols.meaning: position basis labels on each axis
coin qubits; each sets the hop direction along its axis
static random coin rotation angles per site and per coin qubit
probability of finding the walker at B after T steps

equations.label: Disordered coin
equations.description: Per-site rotation of each coin qubit, built as multiplexed Ry(2\theta) gates controlled on the position registers.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions disorder but gives no coin form; this is the proposed concrete construction.
assumptions: Uniform random angles from a fixed seed

equations.label: Shift
equations.description: Coin-controlled increment or decrement on each axis, with periodic boundaries.
equations.justification: A standard 2D discrete-time walk shift with this coin encoding is assumed.

equations.label: Reflecting cut
equations.latex: R=\sum_{(x,y)\in L}|x,y\rangle\langle x,y|\otimes X_{c}\ \text{on the cut-crossing coin value},\quad U=S'\,R\,C
equations.description: On cut sites with the coin pointing across the cut link, flip the coin and skip the hop (reflection). S' is the shift restricted to non-reflected components. Equivalently, a swap of coin direction takes the place of the hop on cut links.
equations.abstract_quote: by cutting some of the links
equations.justification: The abstract says links are cut; reflection rather than loss of amplitude is the sketch's assumption. The exact reflecting-link implementation is not given in the abstract and must be defined unitarily.
assumptions: The cut set L is the horizontal links along y=0 between A and B
Unitarity requires the reflected component to receive no shift

equations.label: Walk evolution
equations.description: T repeated applications of the same step operator with the same disorder realization on the initial state.
equations.justification: Fixed initial state at A, prepared with X gates only, or the trivial all-zero state.
assumptions: The initial coin state is a fixed choice

equations.label: Arrival probability
equations.description: Position-register marginal at B, estimated from counts or read exactly from the statevector.
equations.justification: The readout defined by the task sketch. The comparison is P_B(cut) versus P_B(uncut) with identical disorder.
assumptions: Little-endian: counts bits[::-1][i] is classical bit i

registers.name: coin
registers.role: c_x on qubit 4, c_y on qubit 5

specification.initial_state: |x=0,y=0>|c_x=0,c_y=0>, or a fixed coin state set by X gates

steps.description: Prepare the walker at A with X gates only where needed.
Apply the disordered coin as multiplexed Ry gates controlled on the position registers.

Apply the reflection on the cut line (multi-controlled X on the coin qubit), then the shift for non-reflected components, using increment/decrement from cascaded multi-controlled X gates. Repeat for T steps. Build the uncut baseline by omitting R with the same angles.
Measure the position qubits only, or read the statevector, and compute P_B(T) for cut and uncut. Scan T for the arrival-time scaling.

specification.measurement: Measure the 4 position qubits only into 4 classical bits; the coin is not measured.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Marginalize counts onto position B, divide by the shot count to get P_B(T), compare cut versus uncut, and locate the arrival time peak versus A-B distance.
assumptions: Concrete 4x4 lattice with A and B on the x axis
The 2-qubit coin has one qubit per axis
Reflection, not absorption, on cut links
Disorder is a fixed seed and the same for cut and uncut circuits
No black box or oracle query is used
missing_information: The paper's exact coin and shift definitions (split-step ordering)
The precise cut geometry and the coin-reflection rule for cut links
Hamiltonian realization and winding number formula
